builds.howItPlays: You flood the board with 2-cost units like Punching Poro, discarding spare cards to give them +1 Might, while spells that return enemy units to their owner's hand or deal damage to them clear the way for you to score points. Whenever you start a turn with one card or fewer in hand, Jinx draws you a new one, and Dunebreaker (7 cost) enters ready to attack if you hold two or fewer cards.
builds.whyYou: You like taking the fight to your opponent early, but you want to pick your moments rather than throw everything forward at once. You enjoy the small calls this deck asks for each turn: which card to discard, which enemy unit to send back to its owner's hand, when to empty your hand so Jinx refills it. You don't mind that your cheap units can look small late in a game, because by then you plan to be a point or two from winning. If quick games where even the cards you throw away earn their keep sound fun, this Jinx suits you.

Adjustments: complexity +0.5 on all three (the Legend and Dunebreaker reward timing discards to land on one card in hand); variance -0.5 on all three (the Legend draws most turns once the hand is empty; Zaun Warrens loots on conquer); pace +0.5 on Meuktwo's list (the Legend rewards dumping cards fast). Deciding cards: pace from a wall of 2-cost units (Punching Poro, Traveling Merchant, Shadow Order Disciple, Vi, Destructive, Chemtech Enforcer), Flame Chompers (3 cost, playable for one Fury when discarded) and Dunebreaker entering ready; stance from bounce and burn (Gust, Falling Star, Rebuke, Star-Crossed, Super Mega Death Rocket!) used to clear blockers rather than attacking blindly, which keeps it below the old 8.5; complexity from discard outlets (Poro's Empower, Zed, From the Shadows, Get Excited!, Jinx, Rebel readying on discard) timed against the Legend draw; variance from the Legend refill and recurring Super Mega Death Rocket!. Champion splits between Jinx, Rebel (Devin, Meuktwo) and Jinx, Demolitionist with Rhasa the Sunderer (Trystan). Legend ability: at the start of your Beginning Phase, draw 1 if you have one or fewer cards in your hand. Also played: Hidden Jinx (Jinx, Demolitionist with Hidden units Evelynn, Pyke, Returned and Rengar, Unseen carrying Edge of Night, Long Sword and Blighted Battleaxe; scored Aggro 7.5/7/7/5, two RQ Best of Jinx lists from June plus a 2026-09-23 list) https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/7b6ba13e-d084-407a-9c76-1f1d54d268ed https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/adf5d38e-4c4b-4797-94a5-a8ab67eca140 https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/eb745f5b-8b1a-4d08-953a-f19b1851de81 https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/7012fabb-bdfe-4b74-ba67-0a960b0d42f9. Detonator Jinx (Jinx, Rebel making gear for Detonate, Battering Ram and Rhasa; Midrange 5/5.5/6.5/3.5, one deck) https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/d1534d48-4f33-4553-91e9-ca061ea7ce1e. Confidence: medium. Check: only 3 legal decks in the style. The Hidden Jinx RQ lists predate Vendetta, and the post-ban Los Angeles RQ (2026-09-25 to 27) may shift the picture. Devin's list reads Tempo on its own; if outside labels agree on Tempo, a relabel is worth a look.
